w:r.w:t: Supplier requests deletion of this requirement as "fitness for purpose" and "merchantable quality" are broad concepts that are not appropriate for the supply of complex off-the-shelf electrical equipment. The Supplier's obligations should be limited to compliance with the agreed specifications, Minimum Performance Criteria and the express warranties provided under the Contract.

Supplier requests for inclusion of the proposed wording. As currently drafted, Acceptance is linked to completion of Acceptance Tests by the Principal, which is an event outside the Supplier's control. This creates an open-ended Acceptance date, resulting in uncertainty for both scope close-out and accounting purposes.
We request to add the proposed wording to ensure that the sites are restricted within Australia.

The proposed amendments clarify that a Defect relates to a material non-conformance that impacts the Equipment's or Services' compliance with the Contract. This provides greater certainty regarding the operation of the defect rectification provisions and ensures that the defect regime remains focused on issues that materially affect contractual performance.

We request the inclusion of shipping disruptions and perils of the sea within the definition of Force Majeure. Given the marine transportation and global supply chain risks associated with the supply of the Goods, events such as port closures, vessel unavailability, shipping route disruptions and maritime casualties may materially impact performance despite being beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party. Inclusion of this wording appropriately allocates such risks and reflects current market practice for international supply contracts.

Supplier requests the deletion of the proposed wording, as clause 14.1 contains no asset life requirement. Further, asset life is dependent on numerous factors beyond the Supplier's control and is not typically incorporated into the definition of Good Industry Practice.

Request the proposed amendment to ensure the definition reflects the elevated standard of fault intended by the concept of gross negligence. The revised wording applies on a mutual basis and clarifies that gross negligence requires a serious departure from the standard of care reasonably expected in the relevant circumstances.

Supplier requests the proposed amendments. The current definition is extremely broad and captures indirect losses, unquantified future liabilities, insurance-related costs and other potentially remote forms of loss. The proposed wording provides a clearer and more proportionate allocation of risk by limiting recovery to direct losses actually suffered and reasonable associated costs.

Supplier respectfully requests deletion of the Parent Company Guarantee requirement, as ABB Australia does not provide Parent Company Guarantees and has the financial standing and capability to support performance of its obligations under the Contract.

The proposed amendment clarifies the distinction between contract-specific deliverables developed for the Principal and the Supplier's pre-existing intellectual property, know-how, technology and improvements. This ensures that ownership of deliverables created specifically for the Principal is preserved, while allowing the Supplier to retain and continue using its underlying intellectual property, methodologies and developments developed in the course of its business.

Supplier requests the proposed amendments to ensure that Wilful Default is limited to deliberate misconduct or reckless disregard of contractual obligations and does not capture ordinary contractual disputes, errors of judgment or good faith decisions. The proposed wording provides a clear and appropriately high threshold consistent with the serious nature of a Wilful Default carve-out.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment to limit the class of third-party beneficiaries to those with a legitimate interest in the performance of the Contract. The current drafting extends contractual rights to a broad range of non-contracting parties and should, at a minimum, remain subject to the Contract's agreed liability limitations and exclusions.

Supplier requests amendment so that any further term may only be granted by mutual written agreement between the parties. This provides certainty that both parties remain aligned on the commercial and operational arrangements applicable to the extension period.

Supplier requests the proposed amendments. As the Contract operates as a long-term standing offer arrangement, the Supplier requires flexibility to manage changes in product availability, manufacturing capacity, supply chain conditions, delivery lead times and other circumstances that may arise during the Term. The proposed wording provides reasonable protection by ensuring future Supply Orders are subject to the Supplier's then-current commercial and operational capabilities and does not oblige the Supplier to accept orders that it cannot reasonably fulfil.
Correcting the right reference number of the Contract Particulars.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment as the Agreement operates on a standing offer basis. The proposed wording provides a reasonable mechanism to ensure that future Supply Orders remain consistent with the agreed contractual framework and the Supplier's then-current ability to perform, including with respect to delivery requirements, capacity constraints and product availability.

As per standard industry practice, any such Discrepancy shall first be evaluated based on the order of precedence, failing which the Principal can issue directions as per its discretion to which the Supplier shall have reasonable grounds of appeal, if needed.
Supplier requests mutuality of these obligations to ensure both parties are held to consistent standards in respect of Modern Slavery and Human Rights compliance.
Supplier requests these obligations apply equally to both parties, as compliance with applicable sanctions laws and regulations is a responsibility shared by all parties to the Contract.

We request inclusion of the proposed wording, as the Supplier is required to flow down these compliance obligations through its contracts in accordance with its procurement and compliance policies. In addition, similar compliance obligations elsewhere in the Agreement currently apply only to the Supplier, and the proposed wording provides a more balanced and consistent allocation of responsibilities.

We request that this provision be amended to provide equivalent termination rights to both parties, as each party is subject to the same compliance obligations and should have access to the same remedies in the event of a material breach.

We request inclusion of the proposed wording to clarify that any Direction issued by the Principal must be consistent with, and authorised by, the Contract. As currently drafted, the provision could be interpreted broadly and may inadvertently extend the Supplier's obligations beyond the agreed scope.

We request deletion of this provision, as there may be circumstances where ambiguities, inaccuracies or insufficiencies in the Disclosed Information give rise to a valid Claim under the Contract. Any entitlement or remedy should be assessed in accordance with the Contract and the specific circumstances on a case by case basis, rather than being excluded through a blanket waiver.
Request for deletion as the supplier’s obligation shall end at removal of the Employee from any performance in connection with this Contract.
BG Template provided separately for prior approval and incorporation into schedule 8.

Supplier requests deletion of the Retention Monies provisions. Given the availability of Performance Security and the other protections afforded to the Principal under the Contract, Retention Monies would constitute an additional and duplicative form of security.

As stated in the earlier comments, Supplier respectfully requests deletion of the Parent Company Guarantee requirement, as ABB Australia does not provide Parent Company Guarantees and has the financial standing and capability to support performance of its obligations under the Contract

We request deletion of this provision, as the early submission of Supplier Documents does not impose any additional obligation on the Principal. Further, given the accelerated delivery requirements contemplated under the Contract, the Supplier may need to submit documents ahead of the prescribed date to facilitate timely review and project execution.

We request deletion of this provision. While the Principal's review or approval of a Supplier Document should not, of itself, give rise to a Claim, it should also not operate to exclude a Claim that may otherwise arise under the Contract based on the particular facts and circumstances on a case to case basis.

Supplier requests the proposed amendments as the Supplier's Background IP comprises the Supplier's proprietary technology, know-how, software and other intellectual property. The licence should be limited to the rights reasonably required to install, operate, maintain and repair the Equipment. Transferable, sublicensable and commercialisation rights are not appropriate for the supply of off-the-shelf equipment and could permit use of the Supplier's technology beyond the intended purpose of the Contract.

We request the proposed amendment, as Project IP may comprise or incorporate the Supplier's proprietary technology, know-how, methodologies and other intellectual property, which the Supplier is not in a position to assign to the Principal. The proposed licence provides the Principal with the rights required to use the Project IP for the purposes contemplated by the Contract while preserving ownership of the Supplier's intellectual property.

We request deletion of this requirement. The Supplier is subject to contractual and internal confidentiality obligations in respect of persons to whom Confidential Information may be disclosed, and obtaining separate confidentiality undertakings from each recipient would create an unnecessary administrative burden without providing any additional practical protection to the Principal.

We request deletion of this provision. The Supplier remains fully responsible for its obligations and warranties under the Contract and warrants the Equipment as a whole. Separate warranties from subcontractors are unnecessary and may not be available from all subcontractors engaged by the Supplier.

As explained in previous points, Supplier requests deletion of this requirement as "fitness for purpose" is a broad concept that is not appropriate for the supply of complex off-the-shelf electrical equipment. The Supplier's obligations should be limited to compliance with the agreed specifications, Minimum Performance Criteria and the express warranties provided under the Contract.

We request deletion of the reference to latent Defects. The Supplier's obligations in respect of defects are comprehensively addressed through the warranty provisions of the Contract, and a separate warranty regarding latent Defects is unnecessary and may create uncertainty regarding the scope and duration of the Supplier's obligations.

Request that "life expectancy" be replaced with "design life" as specified in the Scope of Work. "Life expectancy" is a broad and subjective concept that may be influenced by factors beyond the Supplier's control, whereas "design life" is an objective and measurable engineering criterion which is a part of the Scope of Work document.
Weekly updates to Program are not standard and considered unnecessary, we request for deletion.

We request deletion of this provision, as the Program is the agreed planning and scheduling tool for the Contract and provides the basis for assessing progress, time impacts and any associated entitlement to relief. Disregarding the Program for claim assessment purposes creates uncertainty as to the basis on which time-related matters will be evaluated.
It will be Supplier’s obligation to accelerate to meet the Delivery Date if required and in such instances, Principal should be required to assist the Supplier.

For any suspension directed by the Principal for convenience, the Principal shall reimburse the Supplier for all costs, expenses and impacts reasonably incurred as a result of the suspension, including demobilisation, remobilisation, storage, standby and delay-related costs. The Supplier shall be entitled to a corresponding extension of time and equitable adjustment to the Supply Order Sum. If such suspension continues for more than 90 days, the Supplier may, by notice to the Principal, terminate the affected Supply Order and recover its reasonable costs arising from such termination.

We request deletion of this clause, as the Supplier's obligations under this Contract are limited to the supply of Equipment. Installation, erection and commissioning activities will not form part of the Supplier's scope, other than any limited training or technical assistance expressly specified / elected in the relevant Supply Order.

We request the proposed amendment as the current drafting links Acceptance to an action required to be performed by the Principal. Absent a deemed acceptance mechanism, Acceptance may be delayed indefinitely, leaving the Supplier exposed to ongoing uncertainty.

We request deletion of this provision, as the Supplier's scope under this Contract is limited to the supply of Equipment. Site-based services, manpower requirements and related site arrangements are not contemplated other than any limited training or technical assistance expressly agreed in the relevant Supply Order.

Supplier requests deletion of this provision, as it relates to assembly, erection, installation and commissioning activities that do not form part of the Supplier's scope under this supply-only arrangement. The Supplier's obligations will be limited to the supply of Equipment and any expressly agreed ancillary services.

We request the proposed amendment as delays may arise due to site readiness, access restrictions or other matters outside the Supplier's control. The Supplier should not be required to bear storage, handling, financing or remobilisation costs resulting from Principal-caused delay.

Supplier requests inclusion of the proposed wording to ensure that Delay Liquidated Damages are only retained where a delay has ultimately occurred. Where the Supplier achieves Delivery by the applicable Date for Delivery, any Delay Liquidated Damages previously imposed should be refunded to reflect the actual contractual position.

Supplier requests inclusion of the proposed wording to ensure that Delay Liquidated Damages operate as the agreed and exclusive remedy for delay. This preserves the parties' agreed allocation of risk and provides certainty as to the Supplier's liability in respect of delayed Delivery.

We request the proposed amendment. If Delay Liquidated Damages are found to be unenforceable and replaced by a claim for general damages, such damages should remain subject to the same liability allocation and limitations that would otherwise have applied to the Delay Liquidated Damages regime.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment to align with the Supplier's standard warranty offering, which is limited to the repair, rectification or replacement of defective Equipment, together with the direct costs of undertaking such work. Any indirect, consequential or broader remedial works costs fall outside the intended scope of the warranty remedy.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment as temporary solutions may not always be technically feasible, safe or compatible with the Equipment and associated warranty requirements. The Supplier should retain discretion to assess the requested temporary solution and decline implementation where it cannot reasonably be achieved. Where a temporary solution is requested by the Principal and agreed by the Supplier, any associated costs and schedule impacts should be borne by the Principal as a Variation.
We request the proposed amendment to incorporate standard warranty exclusions for matters outside the Supplier's control.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment, as the omission of Supplier Scope may adversely impact the Supplier's recovery of costs incurred in planning, resourcing and administering the omitted work. Reasonable overhead costs should therefore remain recoverable.

Supplier requests deletion of “immediately”, as when read together with the claim bar mechanism under clause 20.5, this may have the effect of barring a valid Variation entitlement unless notice is given immediately. The prescribed notice period should provide the applicable timeframe for notification, to ensure certainty and avoid an unintended immediate bar to entitlement.

Supplier requests deletion of this provision. The Contract Sum has been established taking into account the customs duty concessions reasonably expected to be available in connection with the supply of the Equipment. Accordingly, the benefit of such concessions is already reflected in the agreed pricing.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment, as title to the Equipment should transfer only upon full payment of the relevant amounts due. This reflects a standard retention of title arrangement and provides the Supplier with security for payment of the Equipment supplied under the Contract.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment to align the transfer of risk with the agreed delivery point. As the Equipment may be delivered in stages or to multiple locations, reference to the first point of Delivery provides greater certainty as to when responsibility for care, custody and risk transfers

Supplier requests deletion of this provision, as it relates to installation, commissioning, Acceptance Testing and Remedial Work activities that do not form part of the Supplier's scope under this Contract. The Supplier's obligations are limited to the supply of Equipment and any expressly agreed ancillary services.

Supplier requests deletion of this clause. The Supplier does not accept liability for insurance deductibles under the Principal's insurance arrangements. Insurance deductibles are a matter between the Principal and its insurers and should remain with the party procuring the relevant insurance.

We request the proposed amendment as the Supplier may incur significant manufacturing and procurement commitments in reliance upon Supply Orders. The proposed wording ensures recovery of unavoidable costs resulting from a convenience termination.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment, as a default notice should only arise in respect of a material breach. As currently drafted, the provision may be triggered by any breach, including minor, technical or immaterial breaches that do not materially affect the performance of the Contract.

We request the deletion of the reference to clause 25.4. As drafted, clause 25.4 captures a broad range of matters and, if incorporated into the recovery mechanism, could significantly expand the Supplier's exposure beyond a clearly defined and proportionate allocation of risk. The Supplier is unable to accept such an open-ended recovery regime, particularly given the specialised nature of the Equipment and the commercial basis on which the Supplier has priced and agreed to provide the supply.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment to ensure escalation occurs at an appropriately senior level for both parties and to provide flexibility where organisational roles or titles may change over time.

Request the proposed amendments to align the indemnity with market practice by limiting the Supplier's liability to losses arising from the Supplier's negligence, wrongful acts or omissions, and by introducing a proportionate reduction where the Principal or its Personnel have contributed to the relevant loss. The amendments ensure a fair and balanced allocation of risk and avoid the Supplier assuming responsibility for matters outside its control.

We request the proposed amendments as they reflect the extent of liability that the Supplier is able to assume under the Agreement. The Supplier is prepared to provide uncapped liability only for personal injury or death arising from its negligence and infringement of intellectual property rights, wilful misconduct. The Supplier is unable to accept additional carve-outs relating to indemnity obligations, breaches of legislation or licensing requirements, or insurance recoveries, and therefore requests that the limitation of liability regime be amended accordingly.

Supplier requests for the inclusion of a consequential loss exclusion. As currently drafted, the Agreement does not distinguish between direct losses and indirect or consequential business losses. The proposed amendment reflects a standard commercial risk allocation by excluding remote and consequential losses, such as lost profits, revenue and other economic losses, which are often disproportionate to the scope and value of the supply.

Supplier requests deletion of this requirement. The Supplier does not undertake to maintain insurance cover for liabilities assumed solely under the Contract, nor to ensure that its insurance policies respond to all contractual liabilities or exclusions.

Please refer to the schedule 850DCP0036 - Part C (Returnable Schedules) along with the Supplier’s offer. As known to both the parties, none of the Equipment is manufactured in Australia, accordingly the local content and related points shall apply to the Supplier only to the extent of Engineering, Project management and Technical Support is being executed in Australia.

Supplier requests the proposed amendment to ensure any novation occurs on substantially the same terms and conditions as the Contract and does not operate as a mechanism to introduce material amendments to the agreed commercial or risk allocation provisions without the Supplier's consent.
We request for clarification on the intent for inclusion of this provision?
Supplier requests for and requires mutual assignment rights.

Supplier requests the proposed amendments to ensure that any novation is effected on substantially the same terms and conditions as the Contract and that the Supplier is not subject to unilateral execution rights, deemed appointments or payment suspension rights. Any novation should be subject to the Supplier's participation in the novation process and should not adversely alter the Supplier's agreed commercial or risk position.
Please refer to Supplier’s comment on Price Adjustment / Rise and Fall / escalation.

Supplier requests amendment. The current percentage-based valuation methodology is more suited to construction contracts. Variations relating to equipment supply should be valued using actual equipment, freight, subcontractor and associated costs applicable to the relevant variation.
Acceptance is beyond the Supplier’s control, we request for 24 months from the Date of Delivery.

Supplier does not maintain Professional Indemnity Insurance for this scope. The Contract is principally for the supply of Equipment, with the relevant risks addressed through the Supplier's warranty obligations and other insurance coverage maintained under the Contract.
